name: Seattle
tax_rate: City special hotel-motel tax not imposed; 7% King County convention and trade center tax inside Seattle; 2.3% STIA fee at 71 downtown hotels
notes: No city LTAC grant program found; Seattle lodging taxes go to the Washington State Convention Center and the STIA fee goes to Visit Seattle marketing.

funding_docs.title: WA Department of Revenue Tax Reference Manual: Convention Center Taxes
funding_docs.summary: Describes the King County convention and trade center tax (7% inside Seattle, 2.8% elsewhere in King County) that funds the Washington State Convention Center; this is where Seattle lodging tax goes rather than to a city grant program.

funding_docs.title: Hotel and Lodging Tax in Seattle 2026 (Roommaster summary)
funding_docs.summary: Secondary summary showing Seattle's combined 15.7% lodging rate, no city special hotel-motel tax imposed, and the 2.3% STIA fee at 71 downtown hotels that funds Visit Seattle marketing.

alternatives.program: Neighborhood Matching Fund - Community Partnership Fund
alternatives.administrator: Seattle Department of Neighborhoods
alternatives.funds: Up to $50,000 per project for community-led projects including cultural events, public art and community organizing; requires a community match (volunteer time, in-kind, cash).
alternatives.eligibility: Seattle neighborhood and community groups; projects must be community-driven and matched. Confirm with staff whether a business-led event qualifies (typically needs a community group as applicant).
alternatives.deadline_pattern: Two rounds per year; 2026 Round 2 closed Sept 8, 2026. 2027 dates not yet posted; workshops typically run several weeks before each deadline.
alternatives.notes: Largest open city grant for a free community festival in Seattle; Small Sparks (up to $5,000, rolling) is the companion track for smaller events.

alternatives.program: Arts in Parks
alternatives.administrator: Seattle Office of Arts & Culture with Seattle Parks and Recreation
alternatives.funds: $2,000, $4,000, $6,000 or $8,000 for free, arts-and-culture-centered activations of 2-16 public programming hours in eligible Seattle parks between May 1 and Oct 30, 2027.
alternatives.eligibility: Individuals, organizations or community groups with a King County address and Federal Tax ID that present arts/culture activations in Seattle at least once a year; downtown/Center City parks and some playfields are excluded.
alternatives.deadline_pattern: Opens mid-September, closes late October each year for the following summer season (2027 cycle: Sept 15 to Oct 27, 2026, 5 PM).
alternatives.contact: Zach Frimmel, Grants Project Manager, Zach.Frimmel@seattle.gov, 206-963-9226; Arts.Culture@Seattle.gov, 206-684-7171
alternatives.notes: The 2027 deadline just passed (Oct 27, 2026); plan for the fall 2027 window. A free evening glow in a neighborhood park with performers fits the program well.

alternatives.program: Seattle Center Festál / community festival partnership
alternatives.administrator: Seattle Center (City of Seattle department)
alternatives.funds: In-kind venue, production and marketing support rather than cash; Festál is a year-long series of free cultural festivals co-presented with community organizations on the Seattle Center campus.
alternatives.eligibility: Community organizations proposing free, public, culturally focused festivals; partnership is negotiated directly with Seattle Center programming staff.
alternatives.deadline_pattern: No published application cycle; proposals are made directly to Seattle Center programming staff, typically a year or more ahead.
alternatives.notes: Eliav's prior Seattle Glow events at Seattle Center are the relevant precedent; this is a venue partnership track, not a grant.

alternatives.program: Port of Seattle Tourism Marketing Support Program
alternatives.administrator: Port of Seattle Tourism Development
alternatives.funds: Matching (2:1) marketing grants, up to $20,000 (Tier 1) or $10,000 (Tier 2), from a roughly $600,000 annual pool, for projects that attract out-of-state visitors and promote SEA airport, cruise or marinas.
alternatives.eligibility: Washington cities, counties, DMOs, ports, chambers, tribal organizations and nonprofits; for-profit event producers must partner with an eligible applicant.
alternatives.deadline_pattern: Annual RFP, historically released in winter with spring awards (2026-2027 cycle was posted on OMWBE); check the Port program page for the 2027-2028 window.
alternatives.contact: Not listed on the program page; contact Port of Seattle Tourism Development through portseattle.org
alternatives.notes: Regional alternative to the nonexistent Seattle LTAC; a nonprofit partner (e.g., a festival association) would need to be the applicant.

alternatives.program: Open 4Culture (Seattle Communities of Opportunity) and 4Culture Projects grants
alternatives.administrator: 4Culture (King County)
alternatives.funds: Open 4Culture: up to $2,500, rolling. Projects (Arts/Heritage): larger project awards, annual deadline (2027 cycle final deadline March 10, 2027).
alternatives.eligibility: Open 4Culture arts projects in Seattle must be in Communities of Opportunity (South Seattle, CID, etc.); heritage projects anywhere in King County. Projects grants are for individuals and groups based in King County.
alternatives.deadline_pattern: Projects: final application due March 10, 2027. Open 4Culture: ongoing, due 3 months before the event, reopens April 2027.
alternatives.contact: 4Culture general (206) 296-7580; Art Projects groups: Scott Oshima (206) 477-8064; Heritage Projects: Megumi Nagata (206) 263-3474
alternatives.notes: Heritage Projects is a natural fit for Eliav's balloon-history angle (exhibits, talks, vintage balloon displays) paired with a glow.

name: Bellevue
tax_rate: 5.5% city transient occupancy tax (grandfathered) plus $2.50/night TPA fee
notes: 100% of Bellevue's lodging tax passes to the Bellevue Convention Center Authority (Meydenbauer Center) under an agreement running to 2034, so there is no open LTAC application.

funding_docs.title: City of Bellevue 2021-2022 Adopted Budget, Economic Development proposals
funding_docs.summary: States that 100% of Bellevue's transient occupancy (lodging) tax passes through to the Bellevue Convention Center Authority under an operating agreement running to 2034, paying Meydenbauer Center bonds, capital reinvestment and part of operations.

funding_docs.title: Bellevue Ordinance 5005 (hotel/motel tax)
funding_docs.summary: City ordinance governing Bellevue's special hotel/motel tax; no outside grant process is created by it.

alternatives.program: Bellevue Festivals & Events Incubator Program
alternatives.administrator: Visit Bellevue / Bellevue Tourism Promotion Area (with City of Bellevue)
alternatives.funds: Cash awards of $7,500 to $50,000 per event on a three-year funding cycle, tiered by attributable Bellevue hotel room nights (250-500 nights: $7,500-$15,000; 500-1,000: $15,000-$25,000; 1,000-3,000: $25,000-$50,000; 3,000+: $50,000). 60% paid on approval four months before the event, 40% after the final report.
alternatives.eligibility: Festivals and events held in Bellevue that can document hotel room nights; ranked higher if multi-day, weekend-heavy, out-of-region draw, in need months (Jan-Apr, Nov-Dec), and in a focus area (tech, wellness, culinary, multicultural, shopping, creative economy). No formal nonprofit requirement listed.
alternatives.deadline_pattern: Applications accepted on an ongoing basis; decisions issued once per quarter, 90-120 days after applying. Apply at least 4-6 months before the event.
alternatives.contact: jkantor@visitbellevue.com; Visit Bellevue (877) 425-2075; 11100 NE 6th St, Bellevue, WA 98004
alternatives.notes: Best fit for a multi-night ticketed balloon glow; require Visit Bellevue logo, hotel room block promotion, attendee data collection and an economic impact report.

alternatives.program: Community Programming Fund (CPF)
alternatives.administrator: City of Bellevue Community Development (Economic Development / Public Space Management)
alternatives.funds: Reimbursement grants for free public-space activations. Main 2026 round: up to $20,000 per grant from a $200,000 pool; 2026 Winter Activation round: $2,500 to $10,000. Covers program expenses and permit fees.
alternatives.eligibility: Individuals, nonprofits, community groups and small businesses (50 or fewer FTE) running free, outdoor, publicly accessible activities in Bellevue public spaces or business districts. Paid-ticket and private events are excluded.
alternatives.deadline_pattern: Main round opened Jan 13, 2026 and closed early March 2026; a one-time Winter Activation round ran Sept 3-27, 2026 for Nov-Dec 2026 events. Expect the 2027 main round to open in January 2027.
alternatives.contact: Emily Sherman, Public Space Management Specialist, esherman@bellevuewa.gov, 425-452-4270
alternatives.notes: A free community glow or glow-adjacent activation qualifies; a ticketed glow does not. Apply through Submittable at BellevueWA.gov/cpf.

alternatives.program: Arts & Culture Project Grants
alternatives.administrator: City of Bellevue Arts Program (Community Development)
alternatives.funds: Fixed awards of $3,000, $5,000 or $7,000 for arts, cultural and heritage projects taking place in Bellevue; optional BelRed bonus grant.
alternatives.eligibility: Artists, individuals, community groups and organizations producing publicly accessible arts/cultural projects in Bellevue during the grant year.
alternatives.deadline_pattern: 2027 project grant application period is closed as of Oct 2026; the cycle opens each year for the following calendar year (sign up for GovDelivery alerts on the grants page).
alternatives.contact: Manette Stamm, Arts Program Analyst, mstamm@bellevuewa.gov, 425-452-4064
alternatives.notes: Small, but a balloon glow framed as a lighted art/cultural experience with performers fits; apply via bellevuearts.submittable.com.

alternatives.program: Cross-Cultural Center Without Walls grants (RFP)
alternatives.administrator: City of Bellevue Diversity Advantage Initiative (City Manager's Office)
alternatives.funds: Contracts to local organizations to host intercultural events or workshops at locations around Bellevue; 2026 cycle funded 27 organizations for 70+ events. Award amounts not published on the page.
alternatives.eligibility: Local organizations proposing events that bring people of different backgrounds together for active intercultural exchange.
alternatives.deadline_pattern: RFP released in fall (fall 2025 RFP selected 2026 recipients; the first pilot RFP closed March 8, 2024). Watch for a fall 2026 RFP for 2027 programming.
alternatives.notes: Fit is moderate; a glow would need an explicit multicultural programming component (e.g., international balloon teams or cultural performances).

alternatives.program: Open 4Culture
alternatives.administrator: 4Culture (King County cultural development authority)
alternatives.funds: Up to $2,500 reimbursement for arts, heritage or preservation projects benefiting King County residents or visitors.
alternatives.eligibility: King County individuals, arts groups, nonprofits, municipalities, tribes and businesses (EIN required); for arts projects, must be outside Seattle or in Seattle Communities of Opportunity. Prior 4Culture grant awardees are ineligible.
alternatives.deadline_pattern: Ongoing; application due at least 3 months before the event. 2026 round is closed; the next round opens April 2027.
alternatives.notes: Small first-timer grant open to for-profit businesses; usable in Bellevue, Bothell (King County side) and other King County cities.

name: SeaTac

deadline_pattern: Around May 31 of the second year of each biennial budget; off-cycle requests due 10 days before a regular Hotel Motel Advisory Committee meeting (2nd Wednesday)
contact: Maria Langbauer, Senior Economic Development Strategist, mlangbauer@seatacwa.gov
notes: Only municipalities, PFDs and 501(c)(3)/(c)(6) nonprofits are eligible; reimbursement-based; the special hotel/motel tax brought in about $2.06M in 2025.

members.name: Byron Pihuave

presentation.pattern: Hotel Motel Advisory Committee reviews applications at its regular monthly meetings; off-cycle requests are heard at the meeting following the 10-day submission cutoff; whether applicants present is not stated

funding_docs.summary: Application and instructions for the 2027-2028 biennial cycle due May 29, 2026; eligible uses are tourism marketing, special events and tourism facility operations or capital, open only to municipalities, PFDs and 501(c)(3)/(c)(6) nonprofits, paid on reimbursement.

name: Spokane
deadline_pattern: Two rounds per year: late March (events July-June) and early-mid October (2025 round due Oct 10 for January-June events)
typical_open: March 1 for the spring round; mid-September for the fall round
contact: Council Member Zack Zappone (chair), taciapp@spokanecity.org
notes: Run as Tourism and Cultural Investment (TACI) grants through the Neighborly portal; nonprofits, for-profits and public agencies can apply, up to $10,000 per organization.

funding_docs.summary: Announces the spring 2026 round (open March 1, due March 31) with grants up to $10,000 per organization for events held July 2026 through June 2027.

funding_docs.summary: Technical assistance deck covering eligibility, the Neighborly portal and scoring for the 2026 TACI round.

funding_docs.title: TACI Committee minutes, November 21, 2025 (Spring 2026 awards)
funding_docs.summary: Committee approved $81,000 for 15 spring 2026 grants plus $5,000 for Bloomsday's 50th, awards ranging $2,500-$10,000 with the largest $10,000 to The Family Guide, Blue Door Theatre and MasterClass Big Band Foundation.

funding_docs.title: FAQs for TACI Grant Application
funding_docs.summary: Explains the twice-yearly application rounds, that nonprofits, for-profits and public agencies may apply, and that the committee recommends awards to City Council.

name: Tacoma
tax_rate: 2% special hotel/motel tax; 5% at properties with 26+ rooms (includes 3% convention center tax)
notes: No City of Tacoma LTAC application found; Tacoma is not in the Pierce County LTAC grant program, and the city's Special Events Funding ($90K, due Oct 21, 2025 for 2026) is paid from venue food-and-beverage tax, not lodging tax.

funding_docs.title: WA Department of Revenue: Tacoma lodging tax rate change notice (July 2021)
funding_docs.summary: Lists Tacoma lodging taxes: 5% special hotel/motel tax at 26+ room properties (13.6% combined) and 2% at 25 or fewer rooms (12.3% combined).

funding_docs.title: City of Tacoma 2026 Special Events Funding announcement
funding_docs.summary: The city's only open event grant program: $90,000 to 28 organizations at $2,500-$5,000 each for free public events, funded by Tacoma Dome and Convention Center food-and-beverage tax, not lodging tax.

alternatives.program: Special Events Funding (City of Tacoma)
alternatives.administrator: Tacoma Venues & Events; City of Tacoma Events and Recognitions Committee (CERC) selects awards
alternatives.funds: $2,500 to $5,000 per event (historically up to $10,000) from a roughly $90,000 annual pool funded by Tacoma Dome and convention center revenue; covers traffic control, performers, marketing, infrastructure.
alternatives.eligibility: 501(c) nonprofits, organized volunteer groups, neighborhood business districts and councils, educational institutions, tribes, and for-profit businesses producing not-for-profit public events; must be Tacoma-based or hold the event in Tacoma.
alternatives.deadline_pattern: Opens in early fall, closes in October or November for events the following calendar year (2026 cycle closed Oct 21, 2025; 2023 cycle closed Nov 30, 2022). Check tacoma.gov/special-events-funding for the 2027 cycle.
alternatives.contact: Tacoma Venues & Events, (253) 257-5540 (Tammi Bryant listed in prior cycles); tacoma.gov/special-events-funding
alternatives.notes: Most directly targeted at public festivals in Tacoma and explicitly allows for-profit producers of free events; second-year events can also request in-kind City Event Services.

alternatives.program: Pierce County Tourism Promotion Area (TPA) Grant - Event Marketing
alternatives.administrator: Pierce County Economic Development / Pierce County TPA (Travel Tacoma-Mt. Rainier receives the bulk of TPA funds)
alternatives.funds: 2027 Event Marketing category $42,950; Sports Event Marketing $55,500; reimbursement-based marketing grants to drive overnight stays at Pierce County hotels with 40+ rooms.
alternatives.eligibility: 501(c)(3) or 501(c)(6) organizations in existence at least one year; Tacoma is inside the Pierce County TPA (along with DuPont, Fife, Gig Harbor, Lakewood, Puyallup, Sumner and unincorporated county). Required one-on-one meeting before applying.
alternatives.deadline_pattern: 2027 cycle application window was June 5 to July 3, 2026; expect the 2028 window in June 2027.
alternatives.notes: Tacoma events are TPA-eligible but excluded from the separate Pierce County Lodging Tax grant (Tacoma collects its own lodging tax); a for-profit would need a 501(c)(3)/(c)(6) partner such as a chamber or festival nonprofit.

alternatives.program: Tacoma Creates Impact Funding
alternatives.administrator: City of Tacoma Office of Arts & Cultural Vitality (Tacoma Creates sales-tax initiative)
alternatives.funds: $3,000 to $60,000 per cycle (Level A $3,000-$19,999; Level B $20,000-$60,000), up to 50% of program cost with a 1:1 match, for public arts, culture, heritage and science programming.
alternatives.eligibility: Washington 501(c)(3) arts/culture/heritage/science nonprofits, or groups and business districts using a Tacoma-based fiscal sponsor; programming in Tacoma.
alternatives.deadline_pattern: Applications due in March for programming July 1 to June 30 (2026-27 cycle closed March 23, 2026); expect the 2027-28 cycle to open January 2027 with a March 2027 deadline.
alternatives.notes: Significant money but nonprofit-only; a heritage-focused balloon exhibition or free glow produced with a Tacoma nonprofit partner could qualify.

alternatives.program: Community Arts Projects (Tacoma Arts Commission)
alternatives.administrator: City of Tacoma Office of Arts & Cultural Vitality / Tacoma Arts Commission
alternatives.funds: Project grants for inclusive, accessible arts-focused community projects in Tacoma; amounts are in the 2027 guidelines PDF (not stated on the page).
alternatives.eligibility: Tacoma-based organizations or groups with a history of serving the Tacoma community.
alternatives.deadline_pattern: Applications due late October each year for the following year (2027 cycle closed Oct 26, 2026, 11:59 PM via Submittable).
alternatives.contact: Naomi Strom-Avila, Funding & Cultural Programs Manager, nstrom-avila@tacoma.gov, (253) 591-5191
alternatives.notes: 2027 deadline has just passed; target the fall 2027 window for a 2028 event.

name: Vancouver

deadline_pattern: Around September 20 each year for the following calendar year; LTAC reviews in Oct-Nov, Council approves in December
contact: Andrew Westlund, Economic Development Management Analyst, andrew.westlund@cityofvancouver.us
notes: Four grant types (Cultural Enrichment up to about $5K, Large Event/Festival for 2,500+ attendees, Tourism Program/Facilities, Tourism Organization Operating); requires a 501(c)(3)/(c)(6) host or fiscal sponsor.

presentation.pattern: LTAC reviews applications in October and November, about 3 to 8 weeks after the September 20 deadline, and sends recommendations to City Council in December; applicant presentations are not described

funding_docs.title: Lodging Tax Advisory Committee Grant Program Guidelines (2026 update, for 2027 cycle)
funding_docs.summary: Four categories: Cultural Enrichment targeted at $5,000 or less, Large Event/Festival typically $10,000-$25,000 (past awards up to $95,000), Tourism Program/Facilities ($15,000-$40,000 past program awards) and Tourism Organization Operating ($1M-$1.3M/yr to the DMO); no match required, scoring favors overnight stays, off-peak and outside-downtown events.

funding_docs.title: Lodging Tax Advisory Grants Flyer 2027
funding_docs.summary: One-page notice: applications open Aug 4 and close Sept 20, 2026, with a virtual Q&A Aug 19.

funding_docs.title: LTAC Budget Memo (FY 2025)
funding_docs.summary: Lodging tax revenue of about $3M/yr (3.7M in 2023); 50% is committed to Convention Center debt service and about $1.5M/yr is available for LTAC grant awards, with $6.3M cash reserves and a $2.9M debt guarantee.

funding_docs.title: Lodging Tax Grant Program page (links to 2026 award recommendations and scoring rubric)
funding_docs.summary: Program page listing the 2026 award recommendations, scoring rubric and partnering-with-hotels guide; LTAC reviews in Oct-Nov and Council approves in December.

alternatives.program: Snohomish County Hotel-Motel (LTAC) Tourism Grant
alternatives.administrator: Snohomish County Office of Economic Development / Lodging Tax Advisory Committee
alternatives.funds: About $850,000 available for 2027; awards $5,000 to $50,000 (average about $10,000) on a reimbursement basis with a 25% cash or in-kind match, for tourism marketing, promotion, special events and capital projects that draw visitors to Snohomish County.
alternatives.eligibility: Public and nonprofit entities with capacity to carry out the project; projects must fit RCW 67.28.1816 categories and show overnight stays or economic impact. Lynnwood and Bothell (Snohomish side) events are within the county.
alternatives.deadline_pattern: Opens early August, closes Oct 30 (11:59 PM) for the following year; LTAC review in November, awards Nov-Dec, reimbursements from January. A second smaller round has sometimes opened in December.
alternatives.contact: Harry Birak, Harry.Birak@snoco.org, 425-583-1841; Trudy Soriano, Trudy.Soriano@snoco.org; Sarah Strozyk, sarah.strozyk@snoco.org
alternatives.notes: The primary substitute for Lynnwood's missing city LTAC; 2027 deadline is tomorrow (Oct 30, 2026), so otherwise plan for August-October 2027.

alternatives.program: Snohomish County Tourism Promotion Area (TPA) Grant
alternatives.administrator: Snohomish County TPA Advisory Board (staffed by Snohomish County Tourism)
alternatives.funds: Reimbursement grants for projects that produce overnight stays at Snohomish County lodging; no published cap, with a $50,000 threshold that changes lead time. Annual funding; multi-year projects reapply each calendar year.
alternatives.eligibility: Projects in or near Snohomish County that generate county hotel room nights, support the 2024-2028 Strategic Tourism Plan, and include references from two county lodging properties; off-season (Jan-May, Sept-Dec) stays get priority.
alternatives.deadline_pattern: Due 11:59 PM on the first of any month; at least 4 months before the event for requests under $50,000 and 6 months for requests over $50,000. Board meets the third Tuesday monthly.
alternatives.notes: Rolling monthly review makes this the most flexible regional option for a Lynnwood glow tied to Lynnwood Event Center-area hotels.

alternatives.program: Lynnwood Event Partnership (Community Event Collaboration)
alternatives.administrator: City of Lynnwood Parks, Recreation & Cultural Arts (Events)
alternatives.funds: In-kind only: city promotion (Inside Lynnwood, eNews, posters, social ads), staff and elected-official participation, and public facility or space use. Cash grant funding under the Community Event Collaboration Grant is suspended due to budget constraints.
alternatives.eligibility: Lynnwood business, organization or nonprofit hosting a free public event in Lynnwood serving 250+ people with a public benefit.
alternatives.deadline_pattern: No deadline; submit the online partnership form on the city page ahead of the event.
alternatives.notes: Worth securing for venue and marketing support even without cash; the city also says it offers mini-grants for community festivals but publishes no details.

alternatives.program: Chelan County Lodging Tax Event and Marketing Grants
alternatives.administrator: Chelan County Lodging Tax Advisory Committee (Board of County Commissioners)
alternatives.funds: Marketing and operations of special events/festivals and tourism marketing countywide; 2026 round totaled $221,638 across 43 awards, typically $500 to $20,000 per award (events in Chelan and Manson received $500 to $10,000)
alternatives.eligibility: Nonprofits, municipalities, public facilities districts; events inside the City of Chelan and Manson were funded in the 2025 and 2026 rounds; reimbursement-based, must draw visitors 50+ miles, preference for shoulder season (Nov-May) and matching funds

alternatives.contact: Paula Mikkelsen, Chelan County Commissioners' Office, CM.LTAC@co.chelan.wa.us, 400 Douglas St Suite 201, Wenatchee WA 98801
alternatives.notes: Best direct substitute for a City of Chelan LTAC program; a winter or shoulder-season balloon glow scores well on the county's seasonality criterion.

alternatives.program: Partnership in Economic Development Program (community/event grants)
alternatives.administrator: Chelan Douglas Regional Port Authority (Port of Chelan County)
alternatives.funds: Grants of $5,000 to $20,000 to nonprofits for events and projects in rural Chelan and Douglas counties; event funds may only cover deficits; gave $10,000 to the Lake Chelan Wine and Jazz Festival
alternatives.eligibility: Nonprofit organizations; event must draw attendees from outside Chelan and Douglas counties
alternatives.deadline_pattern: No published deadline; commissioners said in 2024 they would refocus the program away from tourism toward community events and smaller municipalities, so confirm current criteria before applying.
alternatives.contact: Chelan Douglas Regional Port Authority, Wenatchee (main office phone on website)
alternatives.notes: Funding exists but program direction was under review in 2024; treat as a sponsorship ask rather than a formal grant cycle.

alternatives.program: Tourism Marketing Support Program
alternatives.administrator: Port of Seattle
alternatives.funds: Tier 1 up to $20,000 and Tier 2 up to $10,000 per awardee with a 2:1 match (Port pays $2 per $1 of match) for marketing that attracts out-of-state visitors through SEA Airport, cruise terminals or Port marinas; 2024-2025 cycle totaled $600,000

alternatives.notes: Usable by a Lake Chelan event marketed to out-of-state fly-in visitors; a chamber or DMO co-applicant strengthens the case.

alternatives.program: Partner co-op marketing and event promotion packages
alternatives.administrator: State of Washington Tourism (SWT)

alternatives.deadline_pattern: Opportunities are posted through the year; Expedia co-op has seasonal sign-up windows (spring and fall).
alternatives.contact: SWT industry team via industry.stateofwatourism.com; Melia Wilkinson (Premier Media Group bundle)
alternatives.notes: Not a grant, but subsidized reach for an event; pair with a county LTAC award that allows marketing spend.

name: King County
notes: Lodging tax is dedicated by state law: at least 37.5% to housing, at least 37.5% to arts and heritage through 4Culture, and the rest to tourism including stadium debt, with no open LTAC application.

funding_docs.title: King County 2026-2027 Proposed Budget, Panel 3 packet (Oct 16, 2025)
funding_docs.summary: Lodging tax revenue is forecast at about $84M for the biennium, split under Ordinance 18788 as 37.5% to 4Culture, 34.9% to transit-oriented housing and 2.6% to homeless youth; the $18.6M tourism share covers Building for Culture debt, a $7M stadium PFD allocation and $2M in contracts (Visit Seattle $1.46M, Seattle Southside $490,000, Mountains to Sound Greenway $50,000).

funding_docs.title: King County Lodging Tax overview page
funding_docs.summary: Explains the 2% county lodging tax and the state-law allocation: at least 37.5% housing and youth services, at least 37.5% arts and culture, and 25% or less to tourism including stadiums, with about $373M projected for tourism from 2021 to 2045.

funding_docs.title: 4Culture Revenue Sources
funding_docs.summary: 4Culture receives 37.5% of King County lodging tax under ESSB 5834 and distributes it through its arts, heritage, preservation and Building for Culture grant programs rather than a tourism LTAC process.

alternatives.program: Projects grants (Art Projects, Heritage Projects, Preservation Special Projects)
alternatives.administrator: 4Culture (King County cultural development authority)
alternatives.funds: Project-based funding for arts, heritage and preservation activities in King County; amounts not posted on the overview page (prior rounds have funded a few thousand to roughly $10,000 to $15,000 per project)
alternatives.eligibility: Individuals and groups with arts, heritage or preservation at the heart of the project; project must occur in King County; groups must be based in King County or partner with a qualifying artist/heritage professional
alternatives.deadline_pattern: Final application due in early to mid March each year (March 11, 2026; March 10, 2027).
alternatives.contact: Art Projects (groups): Scott Oshima 206-477-8064; Heritage Projects: Megumi Nagata 206-263-3474; Preservation: Emily P. Lawsin 206-477-3110; general 206-296-7580
alternatives.notes: A balloon glow framed as an arts presentation or a ballooning-history heritage exhibit is the realistic angle; pure tourism events are not a fit.

alternatives.program: Open 4Culture
alternatives.administrator: 4Culture
alternatives.funds: Up to $2,500 plus a possible Equity Investment add-on for arts, heritage or preservation projects by first-time 4Culture applicants
alternatives.eligibility: Individuals 18+ living in King County or King County-based groups new to 4Culture; fiscally sponsored groups allowed; no food, equipment or capital costs
alternatives.deadline_pattern: Ongoing; applications due at least 3 months before the event; program reopens April 2027.
alternatives.contact: Scott Oshima, 206-296-7580, 101 Prefontaine Pl S, Seattle WA 98104
alternatives.notes: Small but low-barrier entry point for an organization that has never received 4Culture money.

alternatives.program: Sustained Support
alternatives.administrator: 4Culture
alternatives.funds: Two-year general operating support for King County arts, heritage and preservation organizations with an ongoing public program track record; amount scaled to organization budget
alternatives.eligibility: Organizations (not individuals) with a sustained public cultural program in King County
alternatives.deadline_pattern: Letter of interest April 28, 2027; final application May 19, 2027; awards cover two-year cycles.
alternatives.notes: Only relevant if the organizer is a cultural nonprofit with recurring programming, not a one-off festival.

alternatives.program: Tourism Marketing Support Program
alternatives.administrator: Port of Seattle
alternatives.funds: Tier 1 up to $20,000 and Tier 2 up to $10,000 per awardee at a 2:1 match for marketing aimed at out-of-state visitors arriving through SEA Airport, cruise terminals or Port marinas; 2024-2025 pool $600,000
alternatives.eligibility: Washington cities, counties, ports, DMOs, chambers, tribes, nonprofit attractions and nonprofits running events that draw out-of-state visitors
alternatives.deadline_pattern: 2026-2027 cycle applications were due March 3, 2026 at 2 pm; next cycle expected to post in early 2027.
alternatives.notes: The most natural tourism-marketing substitute for a King County LTAC grant for a large glow event marketed to visitors.

alternatives.program: Partner co-op marketing and event promotion packages
alternatives.administrator: State of Washington Tourism (SWT)
alternatives.funds: Subsidized or discounted placements: Premier Media Group event bundle $3,100, 1889 Magazine package with a free $500 social post, Expedia co-op campaigns, Datafy research discount
alternatives.eligibility: SWT member and partner organizations promoting a Washington event
alternatives.deadline_pattern: Posted throughout the year; Expedia co-op has spring and fall sign-up windows.
alternatives.notes: Cost-share rather than a grant; useful once an event has a marketing budget from another source.

alternatives.program: Tourism and Cultural Investment (TACI) Grant
alternatives.administrator: City of Spokane Grants Department, Tourism and Cultural Investment Committee
alternatives.funds: $5,000 minimum to $10,000 maximum per request from city lodging tax for free public events, festivals, sports, arts, culinary and music programs inside Spokane city limits; reimbursement-based
alternatives.eligibility: Nonprofit or for-profit organizations with a City of Spokane business license (or exemption) and public agencies; event must be free and open to the public, in city limits, not primarily a fundraiser
alternatives.deadline_pattern: 2026 NOFA opened Sept 12 and closed Oct 10, 2025 for events Jan 1 to Jun 30, 2026; earlier rounds opened March or June. Check the committee page for the 2027 NOFA.
alternatives.contact: Caleb Stanton, Grants Analyst, taciapp@spokanecity.org; tourism questions to Rose Noble, rnoble@visitspokane.com
alternatives.notes: Visit Spokane's TPA page directs all event and festival organizers here because TPA event grants are paused through 2027.

alternatives.program: Spokane Sports Community Grant
alternatives.administrator: Spokane Sports (TPA-funded sports commission)
alternatives.funds: Up to $10,000 total per organization per year, up to $3,000 per event for event costs, up to $3,000 marketing support, plus equipment loans and discounted hotel blocks via EventConnect
alternatives.eligibility: Local nonprofit and for-profit organizations hosting competitive sporting events that attract overnight visitors; non-sport events reviewed case by case
alternatives.deadline_pattern: Applications accepted November 1 to 30 each year, review in December, decisions in January; final report due 45 days after the event.
alternatives.contact: Spokane Sports, questions via the grant page
alternatives.notes: A balloon competition or race framed as a sporting event could qualify; a glow alone is a case-by-case ask.

alternatives.program: Spokane Arts Grant Awards (SAGA)
alternatives.administrator: Spokane Arts
alternatives.funds: Up to $10,000 per request, multiple awards per round, $166,000 total in 2026, one-year non-renewable project funding for arts and culture
alternatives.eligibility: Artists, nonprofits, collectives, community arts programs and culture/heritage groups based in the Spokane region
alternatives.deadline_pattern: Three rounds each year with deadlines February 1, June 1 and October 1 at 11:59 pm; portal opens one month before each deadline.
alternatives.contact: grants@spokanearts.org, 509-321-9614, 801 W Riverside Ave Suite 100, Spokane WA 99201
alternatives.notes: Fits a glow with a music, light-art or community arts component; three chances a year.

alternatives.program: City of Spokane Valley Lodging Tax Grant
alternatives.administrator: City of Spokane Valley, Lodging Tax Advisory Committee and City Council
alternatives.funds: Lodging tax grants for tourism events and marketing that bring overnight visitors to Spokane Valley; amounts vary by application and Council goals
alternatives.eligibility: Organizations and public agencies promoting tourism in Spokane Valley
alternatives.deadline_pattern: Application period opens early September, due 4 pm around September 30 (2026 round: Sept 3 to Sept 30, 2025); Council approval in December.
alternatives.contact: Sarah Farr, Accounting and Finance Program Manager, sfarr@SpokaneValleyWA.gov, 509-720-5041
alternatives.notes: Spokane Valley is the largest city in the county with an open LTAC program; an event at a Valley venue is eligible.

alternatives.program: Spokane County Tourism Promotion Area (TPA) event grants
alternatives.administrator: Spokane Hotel and Motel Commission, managed by Visit Spokane
alternatives.funds: $5 per room night assessment funds tourism promotion, convention marketing and major sporting event recruitment; direct event grants historically available
alternatives.eligibility: Not currently accepting event grant applications
alternatives.deadline_pattern: Event Grants are paused through 2027 under the new Spokane County and City of Spokane interlocal agreement; organizers are referred to the City TACI program.
alternatives.notes: Listed so the organizer knows not to pursue it before 2028; Spokane Sports is the TPA-funded route for sports-style events.

alternatives.program: Tourism Marketing Support Program
alternatives.administrator: Port of Seattle

alternatives.eligibility: Washington cities, counties, ports, DMOs, chambers, tribes, nonprofit attractions and event nonprofits statewide
